title: Q2 all-hands: exec update + prioritization kit (working doc)
content:
Purpose:
This is the working doc for the Q2 company all-hands and the concurrent executive update. The goal is to align leadership narrative, present a tight set of company-level OKRs for Q2, and leave the organisation with clear prioritization and asks we need the org to act on over the next 8 weeks.

Audience:
- Execs / ELT: concise metrics + asks for decision
- Managers: prioritization and team-level actions
- ICs: clear signals about focus and what will be deprioritised

High-level goals for the meeting (output-focused):
1) Communicate 3 company priorities for Q2 and the measurable outcomes we expect.
2) Surface resource/rollout risks and get exec decisions on two trade-offs: Dedicated capacity commit thresholds and public roadmap pacing.
3) Launch a 6-week prioritization plan with owners and a weekly cadence of 'incubate -> scale -> measure' check-ins.

One-line narrative for exec update (two variants):
- Variant A (product-first): "We will double down on predictable inference for enterprise customers while reducing per-token cost 20% through platform optimizations and targeted model choices."
- Variant B (growth-first): "We will accelerate product velocity into 3 high-impact use cases (agents, embeddings, reranking) while keeping latency SLOs competitive for PLG users."

Draft company-level OKRs (working):
Objective 1: Make Redwood the lowest-latency/most-predictable inference option for mid-market AI apps
- KR1.1: Median API latency (p95-dist) across hosted catalog <= 120ms for 512 tokens on x86 GPUs
- KR1.2: Customer-reported latency regressions <= 1/month (tracked via CNTRL alerts + CS logs)
- KR1.3: 3 enterprise customers on Dedicated with committed latency SLA pilots

Objective 2: Improve inference unit economics for core PLG routes
- KR2.1: Reduce cost-per-1k tokens served by 20% via batching, cache hit improvements and quantization rollouts
- KR2.2: Automated batching warming and cache hit >= 65% on steady-state workloads for top 30 customers
- KR2.3: Publish model/quantization recommendation guide and have 15 teams adopt it

Objective 3: Stabilize Private deployments for regulated customers
- KR3.1: Deliver first Private VPC pilot with KMS integration for 2 customers (on-prem trial)
- KR3.2: 99.9% uptime for Private control-plane during pilot window
- KR3.3: Provide security posture checklist + SOC-like artifacts for 3 audit requests

Notes on the OKRs: these are intentionally bold — top-level owners should push back on KR thresholds if unrealistic. We will convert to team-level OKRs during the Q2 planning week.

Prioritization matrix (for execs to agree):
- X axis: impact to revenue/expansion (low->high)
- Y axis: implementation cost (low->high)
Hot zone: high impact / low cost items (example: improve prefix cache policy tweaks, route-level batching tuning)

Proposed decisions needed from ELT today (explicit asks):
1) Approve reallocation of 20% of infra budget Q2 to Dedicated pilot capacity (decision by EOD Friday). Owner: Rajesh
2) Sign-off on delaying non-core public roadmap items (list attached) until Q3 to protect engineering focus. Owner: Maya
3) Authorize a cross-functional incident SWAT for two weeks to triage top latency regressions. Owner: SRE (Evan)

Run of show (all-hands, 60min total)
- 0:00–0:03 Opening + quick pulse (CEO) — 2 slides
- 0:03–0:12 Exec update: metrics snapshot & top risks (CRO + Product) — 6–8 slides, tight narrative
- 0:12–0:30 OKR framing + prioritization announcement (Head of Product) — 4 slides
- 0:30–0:40 Customer story + demo (Solutions Eng) — 3 slides + 2m demo
- 0:40–0:50 Live Q&A (moderated using Slido) — pre-seeded questions list to cover tough asks
- 0:50–0:60 Immediate next steps & team-level actions (Company Ops)

Slide checklist (Scribe for deck):
- 1x title + TL;DR slide (2 bullets: what we want people to remember)
- 1x current metrics dashboard (cost, latency, MRR delta, Dedicated pipeline)
- 1x OKR summary (objectives + 2–3 KRs each)
- 1x prioritization guide (what we stop/start)
- 1x asks and decisions table (with exec owners and deadlines)
- 1x week-by-week 6-week plan with owners

Communications plan (post-all-hands):
- Publish one-pager to #company and Confluence within 24 hours (owner: Sofia)
- Managers to run team-level readouts in weekly syncs (owner: People Ops)
- OKR conversion workshop next Wed (calendar invite + pre-work)

6-week prioritization plan (high level):
Week 1: Freeze non-essential PRs; start infra reallocation; OKR breakout workshops
Week 2: Dedicated capacity pilot bootstrap; batching/cache experiments start; initial telemetry flags
Week 3: Early pilot results; gating decision for commit thresholds; internal evals for quantized models
Week 4: Implement rollouts for accepted experiments; customer-facing comms plan drafted
Week 5: Measure outcome windows, iterate; ramp successful changes
Week 6: Finalize Q2 checkpoints; prepare Q3 rough-plan draft

Owner table (selected):
- Overall lead: Lina Ortega (company ops)
- Infra budget commit: Rajesh Kumar (finance + infra)
- Product OKRs: Maya Thompson (Head Product)
- SRE/Latency SWAT: Evan Brooks (SRE)
- Customer pilot coordination: Sofia Alvarez (Solutions Eng)

Top known risks + mitigations:
- Risk A: Dedicated commit may cannibalize hosted capacity for PLG customers -> Mitigation: reserve burst pool and adjustable routing policy; measure PLG latency delta before commit
- Risk B: Quantization regressions cause output quality drops -> Mitigation: small-population A/B tests, prompt-sensitive evals on regression harness
- Risk C: Private pilot onboarding takes longer than expected (legal/security docs) -> Mitigation: prepackage audit docs and schedule a 1-week onboarding concierge

Open questions (to resolve prior to Friday exec decision):
- What is a realistic minimal Dedicated commit size that still unlocks SLA pilots? (finance + infra input needed)
- Which public roadmap items can be delayed without harming top-of-funnel metrics? (growth + product)
- Are we comfortable exposing a small set of pilot pricing to early enterprise customers? (revenue/legal)

Rehearsal plan + owners:
- Wed 10:00AM — Exec dry run (CEO, CRO, Head Product) — Lina to facilitate. Checklist: slides, 1x backup slide, 2 rehearsed answers for expected pushback.
- Thu 3:00PM — Full run for presenters + comms team — record for manager playbacks.

Immediate TODOs before all-hands (owners in parens):
- Finalize metrics dashboard filters (Evan) — due Wed EOD
- Lock slide deck narrative + TL;DR bullets (Maya) — due Thurs noon
- Publish comms draft + manager notes (Sofia) — due Thurs 5pm
- Prepare Decision memo for infra commit (Rajesh) — due Fri morning

Appendix: short script for 3 tough Qs (prepare for live Q&A)
Q: "Why move budget to Dedicated when PLG users still drive growth?"
A: Start with data: top 10 enterprise deals spend X and need latency guarantees; Dedicated is an investment to convert those ARR opportunities while maintaining a burst-routing policy for PLG traffic.

Q: "How will we measure quality after quantization?"
A: We will use model-eval suites per workload, measure delta on held-out prompts, and pair every rollout with rollback triggers at quality thresholds.

Q: "What happens to feature requests that are deprioritised?"
A: All requests go into the backlog and a transparent triage doc (Confluence link in linked artifacts). Managers will own the readouts and re-eval in the next monthly roadmap review.

Notes to self (working):
- Keep slides < 12 and total runtime < 60m.
- Push managers to create team-level 2–3 action items, not long roadmaps.

End of doc.
